title: Unutilised CGAS Funds: Don't Let 3-Year Deadline Trigger Tax
description: The Capital Gains Accounts Scheme (CGAS) allows you to defer capital gains tax by depositing sale proceeds. A common misconception is that tax deferral lasts .

faq.q: What is the Capital Gains Accounts Scheme (CGAS)?
faq.a: The CGAS allows taxpayers to deposit capital gains from asset sales into a special bank account to defer tax, provided they intend to reinvest these gains into specific new assets within a set timeframe. [cite: Income Tax India]

faq.q: When does the 3-year period for utilising CGAS funds begin?
faq.a: The three-year period begins from the date of transfer of the original asset (e.g., the date you sold your property or shares), not from the date you deposit funds into the CGAS account. [cite: Income Tax India]

faq.q: What happens if I don't utilise the CGAS funds within three years?
faq.a: If the funds are not utilised for the specified purpose within three years from the date of original asset transfer, the unutilised amount becomes taxable as long-term capital gains in the financial year in which the three-year period expires.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money from a CGAS account for any purpose?
faq.a: No, funds from a CGAS account can only be withdrawn for the specific purpose for which the capital gains exemption was claimed (e.g., buying a new residential house, purchasing specified bonds).

faq.q: What are the types of CGAS accounts available?
faq.a: There are two main types: Account A, which is like a savings account for liquidity, and Account B, which is a term deposit account for higher interest, similar to a fixed deposit.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on a CGAS account taxable?
faq.a: Yes, any interest earned on funds held in a CGAS account is taxable as 'Income from Other Sources' in the financial year it is accrued, irrespective of whether the principal amount is utilised.

faq.q: Can the 3-year deadline for utilisation be extended?
faq.a: Generally, no. The three-year deadline is a statutory provision under the Income Tax Act and cannot be extended. Missing this deadline triggers tax liability.
